name: The History of Rome
blurb: 179 episodes from Aeneas to 476. The podcast that started the genre — start here.

name: The History of Byzantium
blurb: Picks up exactly where Duncan stopped and carries the Empire to 1453.

name: Emperors of Rome
by: Dr Rhiannon Evans & Matt Smith, La Trobe University
blurb: Emperor by emperor, with an actual classicist in the room.

name: The Ancients
blurb: Twice-weekly interviews with archaeologists and historians; heavy on Rome.

name: The Rest Is History
blurb: Frequent multi-part Roman series: Caesar, Nero, the fall of the Republic, the fall of everything else.

name: The Partial Historians
blurb: Working through Rome's early history source by source, with jokes.

name: Hardcore History: Death Throes of the Republic
blurb: A six-part epic on the Republic's collapse, in Carlin's inimitable register.

name: Historia Civilis
blurb: Legions as coloured squares, and some of the best narrative on the late Republic anywhere.

name: Kings and Generals
blurb: Animated battle documentaries: Cannae, Alesia, Adrianople and the rest.

name: Invicta
blurb: Roman military history, logistics and daily life, with period detail.

name: toldinstone
blurb: A classicist answers the questions you actually have: did Romans wear socks? How loud was the Colosseum?

name: Ancient Rome Live
blurb: On-site videos and lectures from Rome and across the Empire.

name: Perseus Digital Library
blurb: Greek and Latin texts with morphological tools and translations.

name: LacusCurtius
blurb: Loeb translations of Livy, Plutarch, Suetonius and Cassius Dio, plus Platner's topographical dictionary of Rome.

name: The Latin Library
blurb: Plain Latin texts of nearly everything.

name: Livius.org
blurb: Articles on ancient history, sources and places — reliable and readable.

name: Attalus
blurb: Sources for Greek and Roman history 322–30 BC, organised year by year.

name: Loeb Classical Library
blurb: The red and green books, online. Subscription — often available through a library.

name: Papyri.info
blurb: Documentary papyri from Roman Egypt: tax receipts, letters, complaints about the neighbours.

name: Roman Inscriptions of Britain
blurb: Every Roman inscription from Britain, with translations — Vindolanda tablets included.

name: Epigraphik-Datenbank Clauss/Slaby
blurb: Half a million Latin inscriptions, searchable.

name: ORBIS
blurb: How long — and how much — it took to get from Londinium to Antioch in AD 200. Google Maps for the Empire.

name: Pleiades
blurb: Gazetteer of ancient places: every city, road and river with coordinates.

name: Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire
blurb: The map you actually want: the Empire, province by province, zoomable.

name: Roman Roads as a subway map
blurb: The cursus publicus as a metro diagram. Inaccurate on purpose; irresistible.

name: Online Coins of the Roman Empire
blurb: Every imperial coin type, with images and find-spots.

name: Trismegistos
blurb: People, places and texts of the ancient world, linked together.

name: Vici.org
blurb: Archaeological atlas of antiquity: sites, roads and finds on a map.

name: Roman Architecture (HSAR 252)
by: Diana E. E. Kleiner, Yale Open Courses
blurb: Twenty-three lectures; the buildings as the Empire's biography.

name: The Early Middle Ages, 284–1000 (HIST 210)
blurb: Starts with Diocletian and explains what the fall actually felt like from the inside.

name: OpenLearn: Classical Studies
blurb: Free short courses on Hadrian's Rome, the Aeneid, and reading Latin.

name: The History of Ancient Rome
by: Garrett G. Fagan, The Great Courses
blurb: Forty-eight lectures from the founding to the fall; the classic survey.

name: Colosseum Archaeological Park
blurb: Colosseum, Forum and Palatine: the official site and the ticket.

name: Capitoline Museums
blurb: The Capitoline Wolf, the Dying Gaul, and the original bronze Marcus Aurelius on horseback.

name: Museo Nazionale Romano
blurb: Palazzo Massimo's frescoes and the Boxer at Rest; the Baths of Diocletian next door.

name: Vatican Museums
blurb: The Augustus of Prima Porta, the Laocoön, the Belvedere Torso.

name: The British Museum
blurb: Roman Britain, the Portland Vase, the Warren Cup, and a selection of Vindolanda tablets.

name: Pompeii Archaeological Park
blurb: The city that stopped on 24 August 79 (or 24 October). Allow a full day.

name: Ostia Antica
blurb: Rome's port: apartment blocks, bars, mosaics, a theatre, and almost no crowds.

name: Hadrian's Wall
blurb: Housesteads, Chesters, Birdoswald and 117 kilometres of "enough".

name: Vindolanda
blurb: The fort, the museum, and the writing tablets — the oldest handwritten documents in Britain.

name: Lingua Latina per se Illustrata
blurb: Latin taught entirely in Latin. The best self-study course there is.

name: Latinitium
blurb: Spoken Latin audio, videos, and a guide to reading fluently.

name: Logeion
blurb: Lewis & Short and every other major dictionary in one search box.

name: Whitaker's Words
blurb: The classic Latin parser: paste a form, get the analysis.

name: Duolingo Latin
blurb: Short, for beginners, and the owl is insistent.

name: Vatican News in Latin
blurb: Hebdomada Papae: the weekly news bulletin in the Empire's language. Maintenance mode, live.
